---

**The headline**

- **The political AI de-rate became a rout, and this time it did not stay a rotation —
- it took the whole market with it.** Yesterday the blue wave priced a *trade*:
- money out of AI hardware, money into AI spenders, the Dow up 3.03% and the Nasdaq-100 up 0.91%. Today the same mechanism ran in reverse and kept running.
- The **Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed -12.25%**, **SMH -11.21%**, **SOXQ -12.13%**, **QQQ -6.49%**, the **Nasdaq-100 -6.36%**, the **Nasdaq Composite -5.52%**, the **S&P 500 -4.36%** and the **Dow -3.44% (-1,833 pts)**.
- **Every one of the eleven S&P 500 sectors closed red** — the rotation of Wednesday had nowhere left to rotate into.
- The **VIX closed 27.14, +63.4%** from 16.61, and the **VXX +30.13%**.

- The mechanism is the same one the 09:50 board flagged, but the tape stopped believing the earnings. Rep. Yassamin Ansari's post on the night of 11-04 —
- *"Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence"* —
- became a **build-out-kill switch** once the state governorships in Texas, Ohio and Georgia put permitting and power costs on the table.
- **UBS put about 30% of the 2028 data-centre additions at risk** (Reuters).
- A report that **Microsoft is delaying data-centre spending** hit IREN specifically, and the Texas-data-centre complex took its own leg down (**Applied Digital -17%, Cipher -21%, TeraWulf -13%**).
- And a *'they're shooting the generals'* framing circulated on the tape — hedge funds de-risking a crowded 2026 AI position rather than re-underwriting it.

- **The dollar volume is the tell.** **NVDA -8.91% on $54.8bn** — the largest dollar volume on the board and, on its own, the heaviest weight on the S&P 500 —
- then **MU -17.77% on $49.3bn**, **AMD -17.39% on $28.1bn**, **SNDK -22.42% on $23.6bn**, **TSM -11.16% on $14.7bn**, **AVGO -10.15% on $15.4bn**, **MRVL -16.63% on $8.7bn**, **LITE -18.93% on $5.0bn**.
- The memory complex led: **SNDK -22.42%, MU -17.77%, WDC -17.56%, STX -16.66%, SKHY -12.85%** — names whose record quarters were built on exactly the spending cycle now in question.

- **The caveat that changes how this should be read:
- this was not an earnings verdict, and it was not confined to the AI complex.** AMD had just reported the **largest and most profitable quarter in its history** —
- revenue **$13.38bn, +44.7% y/y**, ahead of the $13.08bn consensus — and Lisa Su raised the long-term guide on the call to *"more than 80%"* revenue growth in 2027.
- TSM guided to a **record $53.3bn revenue midpoint**. Coherent signed a **$20bn hyperscaler deal**. Arista guided a strong networking outlook.
- **Every one of them was sold.** That tells you the de-rate is a *multiple* event on the spending cycle, not a verdict on the companies, and it is as reversible as Wednesday's was.
- The second caveat: **the defensives did not catch it.** Yesterday's bid names gave it back — **XLP +3.76% → -0.75%, XLV +3.23% → -2.50%, XLF +3.38% → -2.85%** —
- and the banks broke with the market (**GS -6.47% on RVol 2.01, JPM -4.17%**).
- Only **bonds, gold, oil and China held**: **LQD +0.15%, TLT +0.21%, GLD +0.81%, USO +1.93%, GDX +1.37%, KWEB +1.81%**.
- Even crypto did not: **bitcoin -5.65% to below $76,000**, with **MSTR -8.66% and COIN -9.23%**.
- That is a **broad de-risking**, not a rotation, and it is why the VIX moved 63% rather than 20%.

- **The one bright spot was a print, and it was a company print.** **APP +31.01%** on a Q3 beat with a raised outlook and cash generation backing a **larger buyback**, with the broker note flow already stacked behind it pre-open (**Jefferies $430, Scotiabank $450, BTIG $450**) —
- **$7.76bn of turnover, RVol 4.40**.
- Also **U +13.99%** (Q3 beat, robust Q4 outlook, RVol 4.54), **EPAM +21.25%** (Q3 beat and a 2026 guidance raise), **TPR +7.55%** (fiscal Q1 beat and a better FY27 outlook).
- Those four are the only large-cap long-side events on the board, and all four are company news rather than theme.

**Method and caveats**

- **Prices are the official 2026-11-05 regular-session close** from Nasdaq `/info` `secondaryData`, stamped *"Closed at Nov 5, 2026 4:00 PM ET"*.
- **Volumes are the settled session volume** from the Yahoo daily bar, which matched shibui's settled RTH volume **exactly (ratio 1.000)** on the 11-04 session for 9 of 11 sampled names.
- **The TradingView scanner is ~15 minutes delayed and its post-bell values are after-hours contaminated.** This was measured directly:
- the scanner's 16:01:30 ET pull showed **MU at 669.33 (-15.83%)**, while the official close was **653.90 (-17.77%)** —
- the scanner was still showing the ~15:45 print and missed the closing auction. A post-bell re-pull at 16:25 ET drifts again (NVDA 182.03 → 182.94).
- **The scanner is therefore used here for discovery, the gap columns and the universe only.** The earlier 09:50 board was a reconstruction from 5-minute bars for the same reason.
- **RVol is a floor on 194 of the 1,933 tiered names** whose Yahoo daily bar had not yet ingested through 16:00 ET at the time of the sweep;
- their session volume is a partial and their RVol is understated. The published RVol is the settled volume ÷ the trailing-10 settled average, both from the same series —
- **a screener's own RVol column uses a different denominator and is not comparable**, and it is never mixed into a published row.
- **Screen completeness:** the trigger screen is `|chg| ≥ 3% OR |gap| ≥ 3%` on the **settled** move over 3,114 priced US equities.
- Every survivor of the floors was priced (1,933 tiered). There is no unpriced tail and no top-N cap.
- The universe is the **union of the 15:52 ET and 16:25 ET scanner pulls** so that the scanner's post-bell re-labelling of the session cannot drop a name that qualified earlier;
- the residual risk is a name that moved ≥ 3% only in the final eight minutes of regular trading and qualified in neither pull.
- **Catalyst sourcing:** every catalyst line was read from a dated item (Yahoo news API with `providerPublishTime`, a company release, an 8-K or `web_search`) **in this session**.
- Where a name moved without a catalyst I could source, it is published in Tier B or TECH_WATCH with *"no same-session company catalyst verified"* rather than being given a plausible story.
- **Names whose print was real but whose price reaction ran the other way (TSM, ARM, COHR, ANET, EPAM) are labelled as such** rather than forced into a directional read.
- **Not verified:** the proximate cause of **AEHL's +177.35%** (a $119m-cap micro-float with a +103.67% pre-market gap, $421.8m of turnover and RVol 130 —
- no same-session catalyst was found in this run), the reason for **SWKS**'s opening gap and **LMT**'s gap could not be established with a dated source.
- Those names are published with the price and no catalyst claim.
- **`degraded_sources: 3`** — (1) `polygon-io grouped_daily` had not published the **2026-11-05** bar at run time, so the settled volume came from the Yahoo daily bar instead;
- (2) the shared helper **`rvol_fetch.py` produced an empty denominator** on its first run (see Source health) and was repaired locally — **the shared repo copy is still broken**;
- (3) **194 Yahoo daily bars had not settled** through 16:00 ET at sweep time, so those names carry a partial session volume and an understated RVol.
- **The pre-open feed's catalyst column is not usable for this session.** The verdicts in the gap annex come from 5-minute bars, not from the feed.
- **Split artifacts:** **SOXX (-70.72%)** and **ITA (-68.00%)** are forward-split artifacts and are **not comparable across today**; the comparable semis gauges are SMH (-11.21%) and SOXQ (-12.13%).
